title: Too many users
summary: A load balancer spreads traffic across several servers.

lesson.problem: Traffic grew and one server can no longer keep up. Requests slow down and time out.
why: Instead of buying an ever bigger machine (vertical scaling), run several identical servers and put a load balancer in front of them (horizontal scaling).

The load balancer gives clients a single address and forwards each request to a healthy server, using strategies such as round-robin or least connections. Health checks take broken servers out of rotation automatically.
For this to work the servers must be stateless: any server can handle any request, so sessions and uploads have to live in a shared store, not on one machine.
takeaways: Horizontal scaling adds capacity and removes the single server as a point of failure.
Keep app servers stateless so they can be added and removed freely.
The load balancer itself must be redundant (usually a managed, replicated service).
